title.en: 'Unprecedented': Is this the moment US-Israel ties stopped being 'special'?
title.zh: “前所未有”：现在是美以关系不再“特殊”的时刻吗？

summary.en: Donald Trump and his vice president's remarks about Israel have left some wondering if US-Israeli relations are irrevocably changed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At the White House press briefing room, the United States vice president JD Vance recently delivered a scathing rebuke to Israeli cabinet ministers critical of the United States' deal with Iran .

"Donald J Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time," he said late last week.

"If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world."

It was, in some respects, extraordinary. US leaders have previously expressed frustration — even sworn — at Israeli officials in private. But the comments from Vance so publicly putting Israeli officials in their place were unexpected.

"Since really the Eisenhower administration [1953-1961], the United States has tended to criticise Israel behind closed doors, not in public, so this criticism in public is fairly unprecedented," Brendon O'Connor, a professor of US Politics and US Foreign Relations, told SBS News.

The comments, along with plummeting American public sentiment towards Israel and the war in Iran , have raised questions about the future of what has been dubbed as the "special relationship".

Trita Parsi, executive vice president at the Washington-based Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, says the Trump administration is taking the first steps toward "de-specialising" the US-Israel relationship.

"What the administration is doing now is beginning to be what I would think is the contours of a deep specialisation of the US-Israeli relationship, meaning that it is a very important relationship, but it is downgraded to being at the same level as the US has with France, for instance," he told CNN.

In June, US President Donald Trump called Netanyahu "f---ing crazy" over Israel's military escalation in Lebanon. Last week, he said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had "no f---ing judgment" after Israeli strikes targeted Beirut amid ongoing Iran war negotiations.

This may be the first time that a sitting US president has publicly attacked an Israeli prime minister, but it's not the first instance in private. Bill Clinton, for example, is said to have been incensed after a 1996 meeting with Netanyahu, reportedly telling aides: "Who the f--- does he think he is?"

More recently, then president Joe Biden is reported to have called Netanyahu a "f---ing liar" about a Gaza military decision.

title.en: Meet Andy Burnham, Britain’s likely next prime minister

summary.en: Now that British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation, all eyes are on Andy Burnham. The former mayor of Manchester is seen as the favorite to succeed Starmer to lead the United Kingdom.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Now that British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation, all eyes are on Andy Burnham. The former mayor of Manchester is seen as the favorite to succeed Starmer to lead the United Kingdom.

Back in 2024, the UK's Labour party won a landslide victory, the first win in 14 years. The man who led the party to that triumph? Keir Starmer . But just two years later, Starmer found himself under such intense pressure that on Monday, he announced his resignation  .

Outside his official residence in Downing Street 10 in London , he said a successor was to be chosen by the end of Parliament's summer recess in September.

The man widely expected to be that successor is Andy Burnham. Last week, the popular Manchester mayor   won the by-election in the constituency of Makerfield by a wide margin, securing a seat in Parliament. Holding a parliamentary seat is a prerequisite for becoming prime minister.

"Everyone can feel the country isn't where it should be," 56-year-old Burnham said after his Makerfield election victory, in remarks that already sounded distinctly prime ministerial. "From here on I will give everything I have got to make it so. To ensure the name Makerfield is forever synonymous with bringing about the change this country needs, bringing back something we've lost ― hope ― hope for the future."

Burnham is seen as a leading figure on Labour's moderate-left wing and he has decades of experience in both national and regional politics. He first entered Parliament in 2001. Under Prime Minister Tony Blair , he served as a junior minister at the Home Office before Blair's successor, Gordon Brown, appointed him to roles at the Finance Ministry, the Department for Culture, and later as health secretary.

Burnham even ran for the Labour leadership twice, in 2010 and 2015. In 2017, he left Parliament to become mayor of Greater Manchester, a region of around 2.8 million people in the north of England. He since won reelection twice, most recently getting nearly two-thirds of the vote.

Among Burnham's most notable achievements in Manchester is the expansion of affordable public transportation. Housing and health care have also been central priorities throughout his time as mayor. He is critical of Brexit, the UK's exit from the European Union in 2020, and describes himself as an advocate of "pro-business socialism."

During the COVID pandemic, Burnham locked horns with then-Prime Minister Boris Johnson, demanding greater financial support for businesses and workers affected by lockdown restrictions. The confrontation, and his general success in Manchester, earned him the nickname "King of the North."

title.en: Clive Davis, music mogul behind Whitney Houston and Bruce Springsteen, dies aged 94
title.zh: 惠特妮·休斯顿和布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀等音乐巨头克莱夫·戴维斯去世，享年94岁

summary.en: Clive Davis, the influential music executive known for his work with artists like Whitney Houston, Bruce Springsteen, Billy Joel, Pink Floyd, Alicia Keys, and Aerosmith, has passed away at the age of 94.
summary.zh: 曾与惠特妮·休斯顿、布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀、比利·乔尔、平克·弗洛伊德、艾丽西亚·凯斯和空中铁匠乐队等艺人合作的著名音乐高管克莱夫·戴维斯去世，享年94岁。

body.en:
Clive Davis, one of the most influential music executives in the history of rock and pop, has died at the age of 94.

A former head of Columbia and Arista Records, he signed and shaped the careers of artists including Aretha Franklin, Bruce Springsteen, Billy Joel, Whitney Houston, Santana, Janis Joplin, Christina Aguilera, Alicia Keys and many others.

He had recently been in hospital with respiratory problems and was recovering at home in Manhattan, New York, when he died, his family said.

"To the world, our father was the iconic music legend whose vision, instincts, and relentless pursuit of excellence shaped the soundtrack of countless lives," they said in a statement.

"He discovered, mentored, and championed the greatest artists in modern music history, leaving an indelible mark on culture that will endure for generations.

"To his family, Clive was Dad and Granddaddy, the steady presence at the centre of our lives, the source of wisdom, strength, encouragement, and unconditional love."

"Thanking Clive Davis for transforming music, and on a very personal note, for believing in me, shepherding my efforts and a half century of your love and support," she posted on Instagram following news of his death.

Born in Brooklyn on 4 April, 1932, he grew up in the Crown Heights neighbourhood.

He graduated from Harvard Law School and had no knowledge of the music industry when he took a job at Columbia Records at the age of 28 - but he took night classes to educate himself on copyright law, contracts and litigation.

Davis used that knowledge to help defeat a federal antitrust suit over Columbia's mail-order record club; and successfully persuaded Bob Dylan to remain with the label, after his original deal became void when the singer turned 21.

He was promoted to vice president of the record label in 1965 and shortly after became president. Among the acts he signed were Santana, Aerosmith, Pink Floyd and Springsteen, giving the label a new lease of life.

"Whether there was a natural ear that was triggered, I don't know the answer to that. But when you see a Joplin or a Springsteen, you know."

Davis had a reputation for supporting artists, but his decisions could sometimes ruffle feathers.

After a playback for Simon and Garfunkel's fifth album in 1970, he told the "aghast" artists that Cecilia shouldn't be the first single.

"I felt Cecilia would be a hit but Bridge [Over Troubled Water] was something more," he later told Simon's biographer Robert Hilburn.

"Yes, it was a ballad; yes, it was lengthy," he added, in a separate interview with the New York Times.

"But you've got to know when you have a home run. You can't play everything by the rules."

body.zh: 摇滚和流行音乐史上最有影响力的音乐高管之一克莱夫·戴维斯 (Clive Davis) 去世，享年 94 岁。 作为哥伦比亚和阿里斯塔唱片公司的前负责人，他签约并塑造了艾瑞莎·富兰克林、布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀、比利·乔尔、惠特尼·休斯顿、桑塔纳、贾尼斯·乔普林、克里斯蒂娜·阿奎莱拉、艾丽西亚·凯斯等艺术家的职业生涯。 他的家人说，他最近因呼吸系统问题住院，去世时正在纽约曼哈顿的家中康复。 他们在一份声明中表示：“对于世界来说，我们的父亲是标志性的音乐传奇人物，他的远见、本能和对卓越的不懈追求塑造了无数人的生活配乐。” “他发现、指导和支持了现代音乐史上最伟大的艺术家，在文化上留下了不可磨灭的印记，并将世代相传。 “对于他的家人来说，克莱夫是父亲和祖父，是我们生活中心的稳定存在，是智慧、力量、鼓励和无条件爱的源泉。” 他于 1932 年 4 月 4 日出生于布鲁克林，在皇冠高地附近长大。 他毕业于哈佛法学院，28 岁时在哥伦比亚唱片公司工作时对音乐行业一无所知，但他参加了夜间课程来自学版权法、合同和诉讼。 戴维斯利用这些知识帮助击败了针对哥伦比亚邮购唱片俱乐部的联邦反垄断诉讼；并成功说服鲍勃·迪伦 (Bob Dylan) 继续留在该厂牌，而他最初的合约在鲍勃·迪伦 (Bob Dylan) 21 岁时就失效了。 1965 年，他被提升为唱片公司副总裁，不久就成为总裁。他签约的艺人包括桑塔纳 (Santana)、史密斯飞船 (Aerosmith)、平克·弗洛伊德 (Pink Floyd) 和斯普林斯汀 (Springsteen)，为该品牌带来了新的生命。 “是否有自然耳朵被触发，我不知道答案。但当你看到乔普林或斯普林斯汀时，你就知道了。” 他以支持艺术家而闻名，但他的决定有时也会让人恼火。 1970 年，在播放西蒙和加芬克尔的第五张专辑后，他告诉“惊愕”的艺术家，塞西莉亚不应该成为第一张单曲。 “我觉得《塞西莉亚》会很受欢迎，但《乱水之桥》更精彩，”他后来告诉西蒙的传记作者罗伯特·希尔本。 “是的，这是一首民谣；是的，它很长，”他在接受《纽约时报》的另一次采访时补充道。 “但是你必须知道什么时候你能打出全垒打。你不能凡事都按规则行事。” 两年后，他为布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀提供了宝贵的职业建议，布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀最近以 25,000 美元的天价与哥伦比亚大学签约。 戴维斯在观看这位音乐家的早期表演时指出，他很少离开麦克风，并提出了建议。 “我说，‘如果不是的话，就不要这样做......

reflection.en: The passing of music mogul Clive Davis at 94 reminds us that every life, no matter how impactful, has its appointed seasons. His long career, marked by significant contributions to music, now concludes, marking a time of rest after a lifetime of work. This reminds us that Yahweh orchestrates all seasons, from birth to death, and every endeavor in between.
reflection.zh: 音乐巨头克莱夫·戴维斯享年94岁去世，这提醒我们，无论生命多么有影响力，都有其特定的季节。他漫长的职业生涯，以对音乐的重大贡献为标志，如今画上句号，标志着一生辛劳后的安息。这提醒我们，雅伟掌管着所有的季节，从生到死，以及其间的一切努力。

title.en: Former Kenyan justice minister blocked from entering Uganda, lawyers' body says
title.zh: 肯尼亚前司法部长被阻止入境乌干达，律师协会称

summary.en: A lawyers' body reports that Martha Karua, a former Kenyan justice minister, was blocked from entering Uganda. She is representing Kizza Besigye, a detained Ugandan opposition leader on trial for treason.
summary.zh: 律师协会称，肯尼亚前司法部长玛莎·卡鲁阿被阻止入境乌干达。她正在为被拘禁的乌干达反对派领导人基扎·贝西杰辩护，后者正面临叛国罪审判。

body.en:
Leading Kenyan lawyer and former Justice Minister Martha Karua has been blocked from entering Uganda and ordered to return home, according to the Uganda Law Society.

Karua had just arrived at the Entebbe airport to join a team defending her Ugandan lawyer colleague Erias Lukwago, with whom they have been representing detained opposition leader Kizza Besigye, who is on trial for treason.

Lukwago was himself charged with a treason-related offence last week , and his bail hearing had been due on Monday.

On her return to the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, she said denying her entry had been "unlawful and politically motivated", reports the Daily Nation news site.

She said that as a citizen of the East African Community, she should have the right to enter another member country, such as Uganda.

The site also quotes her as saying she had been told she was persona non grata in Uganda.

Ugandan authorities have not given a reason for blocking Karua, although Kenya's Law Society President Charles Kanjama, who had travelled with her, was allowed in.

Kanjama said it was "of particular concern" that Karua had been blocked, despite her travelling "for the same matter and in the same professional capacity" as himself.

"It is difficult to understand why one member of a defence team should be admitted while another is turned away," he said in a post on X, while calling on Ugandan authorities to explain their actions.

Uganda's immigration authorities have not responded to the BBC's request for comment.

Lukwago appeared in court last Wednesday looking weak days after he had been arrested at his home.

He denied charges of failing to report treason relating to Besigye's case and was remanded in prison.

Besigye has been jailed on treason charges since being abducted in Kenya and forcibly returned to Uganda in late 2024. His abduction, alongside that of his aide Obeid Lutale, sparked intense regional debate over legal jurisdiction and human rights.

The Law Society of Kenya on Monday expressed support for "members of the legal profession across East Africa who continue to uphold the cause of justice under often difficult circumstances".

It called on the relevant authorities to provide clarity on the circumstances that Karua had been denied entry to Uganda.

Karua faced several hurdles before she was eventually cleared to represent Besigye - including her initial application to practise as a lawyer in Uganda being rejected.

She was also deported from Tanzania last year to prevent her from attending the court case of opposition leader Tundu Lissu, who also faces treason charges.
body.zh: 据乌干达律师协会称，肯尼亚著名律师、前司法部长玛莎·卡鲁亚已被禁止进入乌干达，并被勒令返回家园。 卡鲁亚刚刚抵达恩德培机场，加入为她的乌干达律师同事埃里亚斯·卢瓦戈辩护的团队，他们一直与埃里亚斯·卢瓦戈一起代表被拘留的反对派领导人基扎·贝西吉耶，后者因叛国罪而受审。 卢克瓦戈本人上周被指控犯有叛国罪，他的保释听证会将于周一举行。 据《每日国家报》新闻网站报道，在她返回肯尼亚首都内罗毕后，她表示拒绝她入境是“非法且出于政治动机”。 她表示，作为东非共同体公民，她应该有权进入另一个成员国，比如乌干达。 该网站还援引她的话说，她被告知她在乌干达是不受欢迎的人。 乌干达当局没有给出阻止卡鲁阿的理由，尽管与她同行的肯尼亚律师协会主席查尔斯·坎贾马被允许入境。 坎贾马表示，卡鲁亚被封锁“尤其令人担忧”，尽管她与自己“出于同样的事情并以同样的专业身份”旅行。 “很难理解为什么辩护小组的一名成员应该被接纳，而另一名成员却被拒绝，”他在 X 上的一篇帖子中说道，同时呼吁乌干达当局解释他们的行为。 乌干达移民当局尚未回应英国广播公司的置评请求。 卢克瓦戈上周三出庭，在家中被捕几天后，他看上去很虚弱。 他否认了未能报告与贝西杰案有关的叛国罪的指控，并被还押在监狱中。 贝西杰自在肯尼亚被绑架以来一直因叛国罪入狱，并于 2024 年底被强行送回乌干达。他及其助手奥贝德·卢塔莱 (Obeid Lutale) 的绑架引发了有关法律管辖权和人权的激烈地区辩论。 肯尼亚律师协会周一表示支持“东非各地的法律界人士，他们在困难的情况下继续维护正义事业”。 它呼吁有关当局澄清卡鲁亚被拒绝进入乌干达的情况。 卡鲁阿在最终获准代表贝西杰之前遇到了几个障碍，包括她最初申请在乌干达担任律师被拒绝。 去年，她还被坦桑尼亚驱逐出境，以阻止她参加反对党领袖通杜·利苏的法庭审理，后者也面临叛国罪指控。

Even when faced with obstacles, the call to defend the rights of the vulnerable remains a profound moral...

title.en: Red heat alerts issued in France, Italy and Spain as 40C temperatures forecast
title.zh: 法国一半以上地区处于红色高温警报，学校停课

summary.en: More than half of France is under red heat alerts, leading to school closures. The health minister has warned that many citizens will suffer as temperatures are expected to peak on Monday.
summary.zh: 法国一半以上地区处于红色高温警报之下，导致学校停课。卫生部长警告称，随着气温预计在周一达到峰值，许多公民将“遭受痛苦”。

body.en:
Red heat alerts have been issued in France, Spain and other nations across western and central Europe as heatwave conditions are forecast to intensify in the coming days with highs of more than 40C.

More than half of France's regions are currently under the harshest weather warning, with hundreds of schools ordered to close and highs of 42C hitting Bordeaux on Monday, forecaster Météo-France said.

Two children aged two and four have been found dead in their family car in the town of Carpentras in south of France, in an accident being linked to the weather.

Similar red warnings have been issued by the authorities in Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Luxembourg.

The rising temperatures are being driven by hot air moving north from the Sahara desert, which is in turn trapping hot air over the affected areas, with forecasters suggesting the conditions could result in one of the longest heatwaves in recent years.

Scientists have said that recurring heatwaves are a marker of global warming, with Météo-France noting that of the 51 heatwaves recorded in France since 1947, 34 have taken place since 2000 and 26 since 2011.

Temperatures are expected to peak in many parts of the continent on Wednesday, with 41C forecast for Paris.

In the capital on Monday, several train lines also reduced services. France's national railway operator SNCF urged "vulnerable" people to avoid or postpone train travel this week.

Some 845 schools in France were shut, while a further 1,800 are allowing pupils to finish classes early, the education ministry said. But more than a million high school students were take their oral final exams for the baccalaureate amid the heat.

A red heat alert is the highest of four warnings issued by Météo-France, and advises people to exercise extreme caution in conditions that are potentially life-threatening.

Dozens of other regions in France are under an orange alert - the second-highest warning - with an estimated 63 million people in total affected across the country.

The full circumstances of the deaths of the children found in their family car in the south of France are not yet clear but they had been returning from a shopping trip with their mother and reportedly found themselves stuck inside the family car with the windows shut, amid highs of 39C.

The local state prosecutor said the precise cause of death had yet to be determined, but "it is probably linked to the heatwave".

Meanwhile, the French government has urged people not to try to cool off in unsupervised areas such as lakes and rivers, after 13 drowning deaths at the weekend.

In the south-west Gironde region, local authorities on Sunday said three people - aged between 80 and 95 years - had died, partly due to the intense heat.

reflection.en: As France faces extreme heat, the health minister's warning of widespread suffering reminds us of the hardships life can bring. Yet, Yahweh's word encourages us that suffering, when endured with perseverance, can build character and ultimately lead to hope. Even in challenging times, we can find strength and a deeper sense of purpose.

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.

title.en: Kenya minister found in contempt of court over US-backed Ebola centre
title.zh: 肯尼亚部长因美国支持的埃博拉中心项目被判藐视法庭

summary.en: A Kenyan minister, Aden Duale, was found in contempt of court for proceeding with construction on a US-funded Ebola facility despite a High Court order to halt the work.
summary.zh: 肯尼亚部长阿登·杜阿莱因不顾高等法院的停工命令，继续建设一个由美国资助的埃博拉设施，而被判藐视法庭。

body.en:
Kenya's Health Minister Aden Duale has been found guilty of contempt of court over his handling of the construction of a controversial US-funded Ebola quarantine facility.

Last month, the High Court halted the building of the 50-bed isolation centre at a military base in the town of Nanyuki until a case brought by a rights group could be heard.

But on Monday, a judge ruled that Duale had ignored the order and allowed the project to continue. He is to be sentenced on Tuesday.

The quarantine facility is intended for US citizens who are suspected to have contracted Ebola in the current outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The plan has sparked a series of angry protests in Nanyuki, which is about 140km (87 miles) north of the capital, Nairobi, during which three people have died as police attempted to disperse the demonstrators.

Among those killed was 17-year-old schoolboy Sylvester Muigai Ndung'u who nurtured ambitions of becoming a priest - witnesses say he was shot in the head, but police told the BBC they were awaiting post-mortem results to determine the cause of the boy's death.

In its court petition in May to stop the construction, rights group the Katiba Institute warned that the arrangement posed "grave and imminent risks" to public health.

The health ministry later insisted it had not flouted last month's court order to stop the joint US-Kenyan building works, because any ongoing construction was being done solely by the Kenyan government in the national interest to protect Kenyans against Ebola.

But on Monday the judge said the government could not "avoid compliance by recasting or re-characterising the ongoing construction", adding that a court order "is not an invitation to ingenuity - it is a command to be obeyed".

Lady Justice Patricia Nyaundi added that Duale knew and understood that all construction at the Nanyuki site had to stop - yet he allowed it to continue.

In recent weeks Kenya's President William Ruto has defended the plan for the US-funded Ebola quarantine site, saying he had received a request from the US to establish the centre and a refusal would be "inhuman".

He also called on Kenyans not to politicise a matter "so serious" as Ebola, asking politicians to avoid "reckless" talk about it.

Kenya, East Africa's largest economy, had not recorded any Ebola cases as of Monday.

The affected countries are the Democratic Republic of Congo, which has recorded more than 1,000 confirmed cases and Uganda which has had 20 confirmed cases - most imported from DR Congo - so far.

The US plan has led to vocal opposition from one of the biggest medical unions in Kenya - the KMPDU - which questioned why the country was chosen to host a quarantine facility for exposed American citizens.

title.en: Fact check: AI fakes around the World Cup spread political narratives
title.zh: 事实核查：世界杯期间人工智能造假传播政治言论

summary.en: Keir Starmer in a Croatia jersey. An Iranian protest against a US strike. Calls to arrest Brazil's President Lula. Adolf Hitler in the German fan section — all supposedly seen at the World Cup. But none of it is real.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 身着克罗地亚球衣的凯尔·斯塔默。伊朗抗议美国的袭击。呼吁逮捕巴西总统卢拉。德国球迷区里的阿道夫·希特勒——据说都是在世界杯上看到的。但这些都不是真实的。 您很可能亲眼见过其中一张图片。其中一些在社交媒体上疯传，获得了数百万的浏览量。 其中一张观看次数最多的照片显示，世界杯体育场内的一名球迷身穿德国队球衣，挥舞着德国国旗，与阿道夫·希特勒有着惊人的相似之处，德国之声的事实核查团队在德国对阵库拉索岛的世界杯比赛后不久就揭穿了这一假象。 我们立即发现其中一些图像是假的；其他的我们很容易误认为是真的。不管怎样，它们都在发挥作用。 全球领先的深度造假和人工智能操纵专家之一亨利·阿杰德 (Henry Ajder) 表示：“这是一项让世界各地来自不同国家、不同地区、不同政治环境的数十亿人同时观看同一场比赛的活动。” “这是人们开始传播深度赝品和人工智能生成内容的完美环境。” 除了更多轻松的世界杯深度假货之外，许多带有政治信息的内容也在病毒式传播。 DW Fact Check 对其中的几款进行了检查，并向您展示了如何亲自识别假货。 在伊朗与美国之间的冲突尚未结束之前，伊朗队就在与新西兰的世界杯比赛中拉开了序幕，并以 2-2 (1-1) 战平新西兰队，拿下一分。但其中一名球员真的用抗议的姿态来标记结果吗？ 索赔：一名伊朗足球运动员举着粉色背包的照片在社交媒体上疯传。一篇获得约 300 万浏览量的帖子写道：“向被唐纳德·特朗普谋杀的 168 名女学生致敬。” 该图像没有显示伊朗世界杯比赛的场景，也没有显示任何伊朗真正的世界杯球员。 在对阵新西兰的比赛中没有发生这样的抗议，而且照片中的球员与伊朗世界杯阵容中的任何人都不匹配。伊朗队的实际世界杯球衣看起来也有所不同。体育场也不匹配：图像中的竞技场看起来与比赛所在的洛杉矶世界杯体育场明显不同；甚至看台的形状也不同。 不过，这个假货背后确实有一个真实的事件：伊朗球迷在洛杉矶比赛的看台上举行了真正的抗议活动，一些人纪念据称在伊朗米纳布市一所学校被美国杀害的儿童。 《纽约时报》等媒体的报道和 Bellingcat 的调查都指出，美国军队可能参与了那次导致 150 多人死亡的袭击。但病毒式传播...

title.en: Iran-US talks to end war beset by tension, mistrust
title.zh: 伊朗与美国就结束因紧张和不信任而困扰的战争进行谈判

summary.en: While both sides claim "encouraging progress," experts say there's a long way to go to turn the shaky diplomatic framework into a durable agreement.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
While both sides claim "encouraging progress," experts say there's a long way to go to turn the shaky diplomatic framework into a durable agreement.

US Vice President JD Vance declared Monday that a "very good foundation" had been laid for a successful final deal with Iran following direct talks between the two sides at a mountain-top resort in Switzerland.   

The talks were the first stage of a two-month negotiating period set out under a preliminary deal agreed last week, aimed at ending the war launched by the United States and Israel on February 28.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote on X that there had been "major progress to end the Lebanon War," in reference to the clashes between Israel and the Iran-backed Hezbollah militants.

He also said Tehran had secured waivers for oil and petrochemical exports, the release of some of its frozen funds and the launch of a reconstruction and development plan for Iran.

While Iran's top negotiators left for Tehran after the talks, the technical team — led by Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi — is still in Switzerland and will continue talks, Iranian state media reported.

The peace process between the US and Iranian officials, however, has been under pressure from multiple directions since before the talks began. Hardliners in Iran denounced negotiations as a retreat. In the United States, parts of the memorandum of understanding faced criticism for offering too much to Iran while leaving key questions unresolved.

At the same time, Israel has continued its strikes in Lebanon, even as Tehran insists that a ceasefire there is part of the interim deal.

The negotiations got off to a rocky start on Sunday , with the Iranian delegation briefly pausing talks after US President Donald Trump threatened in a social-media post to restart attacks on Iran if Tehran doesn't rein in its allied proxies in Lebanon.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, Tehran's chief negotiator along with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, responded by saying that Iran did not take American threats seriously and warned Washington to be careful with its words.

"They better be careful with their statements, our armed forces are ready to respond in a different way," he said on his X account. "Whatever they say, we are the ones who will act."

The exchange underscored the difficulties in turning the shaky diplomatic gambit into a durable agreement.

Kambiz Ghafouri, a Finland-based political analyst, told DW that the basic ideological contradiction between the two sides has never been resolved .

title.en: US-Iran deal: Pakistan's diplomatic masterstroke?
title.zh: 美伊协议：巴基斯坦的外交主线？

summary.en: By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.

The US-Iran deal, serving as foundation for the ongoing talks in Switzerland , marks a crucial diplomatic achievement for Pakistan, perhaps the most significant in the country's modern history. 

"Pakistan was not only able to effectively leverage its relations with Tehran and growing closeness to Washington but also its network of regional partners like Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey," Farwa Aamer, director of South Asia Initiatives at the Asia Society Policy Institute in New York, told DW.

"It gave Pakistan more diplomatic weight and international support going into the mediation role," she added.  

Islamabad also boasts close ties with China — not an easy feat on a continent increasingly shaped by the Washington-Beijing rivalry .

"Pakistan's patient diplomacy was critical in getting the US-Iran deal across the finish line, though its long-term impact will depend on the agreement's durability as difficult negotiations continue," Elizabeth Threlkeld, South Asia director at the Washington-based Stimson Center, told DW.

She lauded Islamabad for balancing ties with the US and Iran while also keeping key Gulf partners and China onboard, and "helping to find formulations that worked for all sides."

But good working relationships with regional and global powers were just a starting point. The Pakistani government has been pursuing a hands-on diplomatic strategy towards Tehran, with Pakistan's most senior military commander Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif both visiting Iran in May 2025, just weeks before the short-lived conflict with Israel that ended with the US bombing Iran's nuclear facilities.

"Asim Munir and Shehbaz Sharif had both traveled to Iran that summer. That is when, in my view, the Trump administration first began to recognize that the Pakistanis could be a viable and trustworthy mediator," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

Army chief Munir, in particular, seem to have left a positive impression on Donald Trump , with the US president repeatedly praising him as a "great fighter," "an exceptional human being" and "my favorite field marshal."

The Pakistani leaders had much to lose with the US-Israel conflict with Iran spiraling into an all-out regional war. Pakistan shares a border with Iran and relies heavily on Gulf trade routes, so prolonged instability could trigger refugee flows, economic disruption, and security challenges along its western frontier.

title.en: UK prime minister Keir Starmer announces resignation following months of party pressure

summary.en: The UK prime minister announced his resignation after facing months of pressure from his party, stating his commitment to ensuring a smooth transition of power.

body.en:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on Monday he would resign, with a new leader to be in place by the time parliament returns in September, paving the way for Britain to have its seventh leader in 10 years.

In an emotional speech, Starmer said he had listened to his governing Labour Party and realised that he was no longer the man who should lead it into a national election due in 2029.

After spending weeks saying he would fight any challenge to his position as prime minister, Starmer spent the weekend reflecting on his political future at his country residence, watching support for him in the party drain away.

In Downing Street, outside his office and London residence, Starmer said he would ask the Labour Party's organising committee to set out a timeline for a leadership contest to find his replacement.

Nominations would open on 9 July, close by mid-July, and if there is a contest, a new leader will be in place by September. He did not mention his rival, Andy Burnham, who is widely expected to replace him.

"The question my party is asking now is whether I am best placed to lead us into the next general election. I have heard the answer from my parliamentary party to that question and I accept that answer with good grace," he said.

After describing the achievements his government had secured in his two years of power, a man who was often criticised for being robotic, became visibly emotional, his voice cracking when he thanked his family for their support.

"When I leave the biggest job in the country I will spend more time on the most important job, being the best husband I can to my fantastic wife Vic who has been a rock by my side through good times and bad, and being the best dad I can to my beautiful children who are my pride and my joy."

Whoever replaces Starmer will become Britain's seventh prime minister since the Brexit vote to leave the European Union which took place 10 years ago this week.

That level of turnover — the highest in Britain in nearly two centuries — underlines the struggle of maintaining the support of voters angry at successive failures to improve living standards, public services and tackle illegal immigration.

The threat to Starmer, which had been building for months, increased sharply on Friday when Burnham, the Greater Manchester mayor , decisively won a parliamentary election to return to Westminster, beating a candidate from Nigel Farage's Reform UK party, which has led national opinion polls for more than a year.

title.en: Europe's 'Trump whisperer' was its bridge to the White House. Now that bridge is cracking

summary.en: A key European relationship with Donald Trump is under strain as he trades blows with Italy's Giorgia Meloni.

body.en:
When Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni was the only European leader to attend the inauguration.

Seventeen months later, their relationship is publicly breaking down, as the two right-wing leaders trade barbs on social media.

Trump's relationships with traditional European allies have further strained in his second term, and he's become increasingly unpopular among voters in much of Western Europe.

He's clashed with leaders including Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his decision to go to war with Iran.

And earlier this year, he shattered trust within the NATO military alliance with threats to take over Greenland.

The deterioration of the relationship with Meloni raises questions about who, if anyone, still has the US president's ear in Europe.

Meloni was viewed as one of the few leaders capable of acting as a bridge between Trump and Europe, dubbed a "Trump whisperer" by some commentators.

But cracks appeared after the US and Israel started a war with Iran earlier this year, triggering global oil price surges , damaging European economies and igniting strong anti-war sentiment in Italy.

In April, Trump lashed out at Pope Leo XIV after the pontiff denounced the war in the Middle East, criticised Trump's threat to destroy Iranian civilisation , and called on the US president to find an "off-ramp" to end the conflict.

Facing domestic pressure at the time, Meloni said Trump's comments about the pope were "unacceptable", prompting a rebuke from Trump.

Italy had also denied the use of an airbase in Sicily to US military planes carrying weapons for the war in Iran, saying the Americans had not followed the necessary procedures.

To onlookers at the G7 summit in France last week, Trump and Meloni appeared as though they might have reconciled.

That impression was short-lived. On Friday, Italian TV channel La7 quoted Trump as saying Meloni "begged me to take a picture with her".

"I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said, according to the broadcaster's translation.

Responding in a video on social media, Meloni said Trump's statements were fabricated.

"I am frankly astonished. I don't know why the president of the United States behaves like this towards his allies. It is not the first time," she said.

"It is disappointing that he does not show the same determination with the enemies of the West and of the United States, whose leaders he instead treats with far greater indulgence. Neither I nor Italy ever beg."

body.en:
A punishing heatwave sweeping across Europe is prompting governments to impose restrictions, issue warnings and reshape daily life as temperatures climb towards record levels.

France is preparing for temperatures of up to 41C, with 35 of the country's 96 regions expected to move onto red heatwave alerts stretching from the southwest through Paris and into Burgundy.

After a crisis meeting, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced restrictions on alcohol consumption at public events, including the annual Fête de la Musique celebrations across affected regions.

Authorities in Paris have also ordered parks to remain open around the clock to help residents escape the heat.

Elsewhere, heat alerts were issued across most of Germany as temperatures approached 38C.

Germany's national weather service warned that a combination of high temperatures and humidity could increase the risk of severe thunderstorms.

In Spain, authorities closed a World Cup fan zone in Madrid's Plaza de Colón that had been set up with giant screens for supporters to watch Spain's match against Saudi Arabia .

Parts of Spain remain under heat warnings, with some outdoor sporting and cultural activities suspended.

In Italy, authorities expanded heat warnings across several cities as temperatures pushed into the high 30s.

Across southern Europe, the heat has reportedly begun altering how residents and tourists move through cities.

In Rome, visitors queued in the sun outside the Colosseum while others sought relief in cooler underground spaces beneath the remains of the Temple of Claudius.

In Bologna, among Italy's hottest cities, people cooled off at the Fountain of Neptune and sheltered beneath shaded porticoes.

French authorities increased staffing across rail services amid concerns that extreme temperatures could affect infrastructure, including tracks and electrical systems.

Officials have also tightened monitoring around water supplies and bushfire conditions.

The government ordered hundreds of schools to close ahead of expected peak temperatures.

Bank of France governor Emmanuel Moulin said the short-term impact on growth was mixed, with reduced productivity offset in part by higher energy demand, but warned that prolonged periods of extreme heat weigh on economies over time.

Health authorities have also renewed warnings around heat exhaustion and heat stroke, particularly for older people and vulnerable communities.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has threatened to strike Iran over its support for Hezbollah.

The threat has cast uncertainty over the opening of high-stakes negotiations aimed at turning a fragile ceasefire into a longer-term peace agreement.

The warning came as senior US and Iranian officials gathered in Switzerland for the first round of talks aimed at building on a preliminary memorandum of understanding reached last week to end months of regional conflict.

Posting on Truth Social as negotiations got underway, Trump said Iran must "immediately stop their highly paid proxies in Lebanon from causing trouble".

"If they don’t, we’ll hit Iran very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder!!!" he wrote.

Iran responded swiftly with chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warning the US to "be careful" with its language, saying Iran's armed forces were prepared to respond and insisting US threats had failed to alter Iran's position.

The heightened rhetoric briefly fuelled speculation that the negotiations could unravel before substantive discussions had begun.

Iranian state media reported Iran's delegation had left the venue in response to Trump's comments, with some outlets suggesting the talks had been suspended.

But that account was later called into question when a diplomat familiar with the negotiations told Agence France-Presse the Iranian delegation remained engaged and had not indicated to mediators any intention to withdraw.

The negotiations, mediated by Pakistan and Qatar at the Swiss resort of Bürgenstock, are intended to launch a 60-day process to negotiate a more permanent settlement and ease tensions across the region.

Iran said continued Israeli military activity and the implementation of commitments in Lebanon would dominate the opening round of talks.

The preliminary agreement signed last week committed both sides to ending hostilities across multiple fronts, including between Israel and Hezbollah.

Yet repeated clashes in southern Lebanon have raised doubts over whether that framework can hold.

Iran has insisted that meaningful progress towards a final agreement cannot happen while fighting continues.

The uncertainty around Lebanon was further complicated by comments from Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, who publicly rejected suggestions his country could play a military role in the conflict.

title.en: US-Iran deal: Pakistan's diplomatic masterstroke?

summary.en: By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.

The US-Iran deal, serving as foundation for the ongoing talks in Switzerland , marks a crucial diplomatic achievement for Pakistan, perhaps the most significant in the country's modern history. 

"Pakistan was not only able to effectively leverage its relations with Tehran and growing closeness to Washington but also its network of regional partners like Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey," Farwa Aamer, director of South Asia Initiatives at the Asia Society Policy Institute in New York, told DW.

"It gave Pakistan more diplomatic weight and international support going into the mediation role," she added.  

Islamabad also boasts close ties with China — not an easy feat on a continent increasingly shaped by the Washington-Beijing rivalry .

"Pakistan's patient diplomacy was critical in getting the US-Iran deal across the finish line, though its long-term impact will depend on the agreement's durability as difficult negotiations continue," Elizabeth Threlkeld, South Asia director at the Washington-based Stimson Center, told DW.

She lauded Islamabad for balancing ties with the US and Iran while also keeping key Gulf partners and China onboard, and "helping to find formulations that worked for all sides."

But good working relationships with regional and global powers were just a starting point. The Pakistani government has been pursuing a hands-on diplomatic strategy towards Tehran, with Pakistan's most senior military commander Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif both visiting Iran in May 2025, just weeks before the short-lived conflict with Israel that ended with the US bombing Iran's nuclear facilities.

"Asim Munir and Shehbaz Sharif had both traveled to Iran that summer. That is when, in my view, the Trump administration first began to recognize that the Pakistanis could be a viable and trustworthy mediator," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

Army chief Munir, in particular, seem to have left a positive impression on Donald Trump , with the US president repeatedly praising him as a "great fighter," "an exceptional human being" and "my favorite field marshal."

The Pakistani leaders had much to lose with the US-Israel conflict with Iran spiraling into an all-out regional war. Pakistan shares a border with Iran and relies heavily on Gulf trade routes, so prolonged instability could trigger refugee flows, economic disruption, and security challenges along its western frontier.

title.en: China's import of custard apples is sparking fears in Taiwan

summary.en: Taiwan's agriculture ministry is worried that Beijing wants to weaponise a local specialty: the atemoya.

body.en:
A scaly, heart-shaped fruit could become the latest cause of friction between China and Taiwan, as the latter warned farmers against Beijing's plan to step up imports of the crop.

The atemoya, a hybrid of different custard apple species with creamy white flesh encased in a rough green exterior, is a specialty of Taiwan's Taitung county.

China, a key importer of Taiwanese atemoyas, pledged to buy more of the fruit earlier this month.

But a press release by Taiwan's agriculture ministry on Saturday claimed this was a "classic example of China's 'raise, trap, kill' process", by which Beijing creates reliance before leaving farmers exposed to market changes.

Beijing claims the self-governed island of Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out taking it by force. In recent years it has stepped up military drills near Taiwan, including simulating blockades on the island.

Observers say China has also engaged in a range of non-military tactics to pressure Taiwan. And one apparent weapon is fruit.

In 2021, China banned the import of Taiwanese pineapples , causing major disruption to farmers' livelihoods. This sparked a domestic consumption movement to counter what many Taiwanese saw as economic coercion.

"First, China makes large purchases to show goodwill and encourage farmers to grow atemoyas. Next it unilaterally imposes export restrictions without warning," the Taiwanese agriculture ministry said in its press release.

The statement noted that China suspended imports of atemoyas in 2021, citing pest concerns, before partially resuming imports in 2023 and then slapping taxes on the fruit in 2024.

Such moves "cause the industry to face huge instability and farmers to bear great risks," the ministry said.

It added that China has also been expanding its own atemoya cultivation, posing a threat to Taiwan's local industry.

The growing debate over the export of Taiwanese atemoyas started earlier this month, after Chinese companies pledged to buy more of the fruit at a forum in China's Xiamen city - a coastal city on the Taiwan Strait. This was part of a broader plan to expand purchases of Taiwanese exports to China, including fish and tea.

The forum was attended by business leaders and opposition politicians from Taiwan, despite an official ban on participation by Taiwan's central government.

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council spokesperson has since warned that officials who attended the forum could be investigated.

In its statement, Taiwan's agriculture ministry said authorities would focus on "sustainable agricultural development and stable income for farmers", and "continue to guide the atemoya industry toward diversified processing", including by producing frozen fruit products, puree and wines.

reflection.zh: 汽油价格在最初警告可能出现短缺和创纪录高位后，意外下降，这提醒我们，焦虑时期可能会迎来缓解。正如哭泣可能持续一夜，喜乐确实会在早晨到来，而且常常是通过意想不到的情况。这一转变提供了一个充满希望的视角，说明挑战可能以我们未曾预料的方式得到解决。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in electric vehicle technology, making them cheaper and more efficient, reflect a remarkable acceleration of human knowledge and innovation. This progress reminds us of the human capacity to explore and develop new solutions, continually expanding our understanding and capabilities.
reflection.zh: 电动汽车技术日新月异，变得更便宜、更高效，这反映了人类知识和创新的显著加速。这种进步提醒我们，人类有能力探索和开发新的解决方案，不断拓展我们的理解和能力。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release
title.zh: 在中国，女性喜剧演员为厌倦性别歧视的女性提供宣泄出口

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...
body.zh: 单口喜剧为女性提供了谈论某些变得更加敏感的话题的空间，而表演者们仍然对审查制度的限制保持警惕北京东部一个小型表演艺术空间的楼上剧场里，有 100 多人（其中大部分是女性）满怀期待。 “你是来看谁的？”身穿褪色牛仔两件套西装的主持人问道。对方齐声喊道：“方主任！”方绍立，又名方主任（方主任），过去两年在中国建立了一批狂热的追随者。方穿着黄色连帽衫和深蓝色牛仔裤，明显不如当晚主持人时尚。她的普通女性着装是其吸引力的一部分。方出生于1975年，来自中国东部山东省的农村地区，身材魁梧，留着一头漂亮的短发。在发现单口喜剧艺术之前，她曾在工厂和建筑工地工作过，但主要是作为一位难相处的丈夫的家庭主妇生活。她的笑话反复提及了渗透在中国文化中的根深蒂固的性别歧视，尤其是在远离北京和上海等大城市中心的地方。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the human need to express frustrations and experiences, especially when facing societal pressures like sexism. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those whose voices are often unheard, advocating for justice and dignity. Even in challenging environments, creative expression can offer a vital space for shared...
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类表达挫折和经历的需求，尤其是在面对性别歧视等社会压力时。箴言31:8-9提醒我们，为那些常常被忽视的声音发声，倡导公义和尊严是何等重要。即使在充满挑战的环境中，创造性的表达也能为共同的理解和释放提供一个重要的空间，这反映了雅伟对边缘群体的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Border Force officer and Hong Kong trade official jailed for spying for China
title.zh: 英国边境部队官员和香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动被判入狱

summary.en: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official have been sentenced to 10 and eight years in prison, respectively, after being convicted of spying for China. These are the first convictions under the UK's National Security Act.
summary.zh: 一名英国边境部队官员和一名香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，刑期分别为10年和8年。这是英国根据《国家安全法》首次定罪的案件。

body.en: Peter Wai and Bill Yuen sentenced to 10 and eight years at Old Bailey in first convictions under National Security Act A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official based in London have been jailed for spying for China in the first such conviction in British criminal history. Peter Wai, who conducted “shadow policing” operations on Chinese dissidents in the UK, was sentenced to 10 years, while his handler, Bill Yuen, received an eight-year term. Continue reading...
body.zh: Peter Wai和Bill Yuen根据《国家安全法》首次在老贝利被判刑10年和8年。一名英国边防部队官员和一名驻伦敦的香港贸易官员因为中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，这是英国犯罪史上的首次此类定罪。在英国对中国持不同政见者进行“影子警察”行动的韦彼得被判处10年徒刑，而他的经纪人袁比尔则被判处8年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound breach of trust when public officials betray their duties. Yahweh's word reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities reflects our character in larger ones. May we all strive for integrity in every role we are given, understanding that honesty builds trust and strengthens the fabric of society.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了公职人员背叛职责时对信任的严重破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们，在小事上忠心的人，在大事上也忠心。愿我们都在所担任的每一个角色中追求正直，明白诚实能建立信任并巩固社会结构。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Inspired by Ukraine, and worried by China: Taiwan teaches its citizens how to fly drones
title.zh: 受乌克兰启发，担忧中国大陆：台湾教导市民如何驾驶无人机

summary.en: Ordinary citizens in Taiwan are enrolling in drone piloting courses, inspired by events in Ukraine and concerned about a potential military threat from China. These courses teach participants, young and old, how to operate drones for various purposes.
summary.zh: 受乌克兰局势的启发并担忧中国大陆的军事威胁，台湾普通民众（包括年轻人和老年人）正在参加无人机驾驶课程。这些课程旨在教授学员如何操作无人机以应对潜在情况。

body.en: Ordinary Taiwanese, young and old, are joining courses to learn how to fly drones amid looming China military threat In a small, crowded room in Taipei, Pan Chien-chin is trying to keep a drone hovering steadily. Imagining himself flying a plane, he gently nudges controller joysticks to guide the insect-like device as it hums through the air. Cheers break out as Pan, who has never flown a drone before, steers it around a rectangular course marked by traffic cones without crashing. Around him are about two dozen fellow trainees, all signed up for the same course: Taiwan’s first civil defence drone training programme. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾普通民众，无论老少，都在参加课程，学习如何在迫在眉睫的中国军事威胁下驾驶无人机。在台北一间拥挤的小房间里，潘建钦正努力让无人机保持稳定盘旋。他想象自己驾驶一架飞机，轻轻推动控制器操纵杆，引导昆虫般的设备在空中嗡嗡作响。当潘以前从未驾驶过无人机时，他驾驶无人机绕着一个由交通锥标标记的矩形航线飞行，没有坠毁，引发了欢呼声。他周围大约有两打学员，他们都报名参加同一门课程：台湾首个民防无人机训练计划。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The story highlights a community's proactive response to perceived threats, reflecting a natural human inclination to prepare for potential dangers. Proverbs reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing trouble and taking steps to protect ourselves and our communities. Such foresight, when coupled with a reliance on Yahweh, can guide us in uncertain times.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻讲述了一个社区如何积极应对潜在威胁，反映了人类为可能出现的危险做准备的自然倾向。箴言提醒我们，预见祸患并采取措施保护自己和社区是智慧之举。这种远见，若能与对雅伟的信靠结合，便能在不确定的时期指引我们。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Lululemon apologises after Japanese drum row at Great Wall yoga event
title.zh: Lululemon因长城瑜伽活动中的日本太鼓风波致歉

summary.en: The activewear brand Lululemon issued an apology after an online uproar in China. The controversy stemmed from a promotional yoga event held on the Great Wall of China, where a Japanese taiko drum was mistakenly featured instead of a Chinese drum, despite the event being intended to celebrate Chinese culture.
summary.zh: 运动服饰品牌Lululemon因在中国长城举办的瑜伽推广活动中误用日本太鼓而引发网络争议后，发表了道歉声明。尽管该活动旨在庆祝中国文化，但这一失误在中国引发了线上轩然大波。

body.en: Online uproar follows Canadian brand’s use of taiko drum at sponsored festival held to celebrate Chinese culture The activewear brand Lululemon has apologised after a promotional event held on the Great Wall of China appeared to mistakenly feature a Japanese drum, prompting an uproar. The Canadian-headquartered company, known for its upmarket leggings, has been growing rapidly in China and arranged for a yoga festival to take place in late May on a section of the wall near Beijing. Continue reading...
body.zh: 加拿大品牌在为庆祝中国文化而举办的赞助节日上使用太鼓，在中国引起网络轩然大波运动服品牌 Lululemon 在中国长城举行的一次促销活动中错误地使用了日本太鼓，引发轩然大波，该品牌已道歉。这家总部位于加拿大的公司以其高档瑜伽紧身裤而闻名，在中国发展迅速，并于五月底在北京附近的一段长城举办了一场瑜伽节。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This incident reminds us how quickly a seemingly small cultural misstep can ignite widespread public sentiment, especially in the digital age. Just as a tiny spark can set a vast forest ablaze, unintentional actions or symbols can inadvertently cause significant uproar and division. It underscores the need for careful consideration and humility in our...
reflection.zh: 这起事件提醒我们，一个看似微小的文化失误，尤其在数字时代，能多么迅速地引发广泛的公众情绪。正如一点火花能点燃整片森林，无意的行为或象征也可能不经意间造成巨大的争议和分歧。这强调了我们在互动中需要谨慎思考和谦卑，认识到即使是微小的细节也可能产生深远的影响。

verse.textEn: The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.
verse.textZh: 舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

title.en: They were forced into marriage and abused. Now women facing exploitation in China have a glimmer of hope
title.zh: 她们被迫结婚并遭受虐待。现在，中国面临剥削的女性有了一线希望

summary.en: Female activists are secretly working to locate and assist vulnerable women in China who have been forced into marriage and subjected to abuse, as they believe authorities are not adequately protecting them.
summary.zh: 在中国，女性活动家们正在秘密寻找并帮助那些被迫结婚并遭受虐待的弱势女性，因为她们担心官方未能提供足够的保护。

body.en: Female activists are working in the shadows to find and support vulnerable women they fear are being failed by authorities Last summer, Xiaocao, a softly spoken woman in her 40s, received a tip-off that in Lüliang, a small city in China’s Shanxi province, vulnerable women were being forced into marriages. Along with another volunteer, she wanted to investigate. After leaving Beijing, the two volunteers travelled south for hours, on trains and in rental cars. A few villages turned out to be dead ends. But on the final day of their trip, the women stopped in a county where they’d heard about a woman with learning disabilities who was “married” to two brothers. Soon, they found her. Continue reading...
body.zh: 女性活动人士正在暗中寻找和支持她们担心当局辜负的弱势女性。去年夏天，40 多岁、说话轻声细语的小曹接到举报，称在中国山西省的一个小城市吕梁，弱势女性正在被迫结婚。她想和另一名志愿者一起进行调查。离开北京后，两名志愿者乘坐火车和租车向南行驶了几个小时。一些村庄变成了死胡同。但在旅行的最后一天，妇女们在一个县停下来，她们听说那里有一名有学习障碍的妇女“嫁给”了两个兄弟。很快，他们就找到了她。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courageous work of activists who step in when vulnerable individuals are failed by systems meant to protect them. Their efforts embody the call to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for justice and dignity for the exploited.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了活动家们的勇气，当弱势群体未能得到应有的保护时，她们挺身而出。她们的努力体现了为那些无法为自己发声的人说话的呼召，为受剥削者争取正义和尊严。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.zh: 澳洲栏目

title.en: What's changing from 1 July? The new rules affecting your wallet
title.zh: 7 月 1 日起有何变化？新规则影响你的钱包

summary.en: A new financial year means new rules. Here's what’s changing for Australians from 1 July.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australians will see changes to wages, tax, superannuation, parental leave and more from 1 July, as a suite of federal and state reforms take effect at the start of the new financial year.

The annual reset often brings regulatory and legislative updates, but this year’s changes affect workers’ pay packets, retirement savings, family budgets and business operations.

Millions of Australians covered by awards will receive higher pay after the Fair Work Commission approved a 4.75 per cent increase to minimum and award wages earlier this month.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The National Minimum Wage will rise to $26.44 an hour, equivalent to $1,004.90 a week based on a 38-hour week before tax.

The increase applies from the first full pay period starting on or after 1 July.

Around 2.8 million employees paid under modern awards are expected to benefit, alongside workers who receive the national minimum wage.

One of the biggest structural changes taking effect this financial year is the introduction of payday super.

From 1 July, employers will be required to pay employees’ superannuation contributions at the same time as wages, rather than quarterly.

The change is designed to reduce unpaid and delayed super and make retirement savings easier for workers to track.

James Koval, chief policy and advocacy officer at the Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia, said the reform would affect around 19 million Australians with super accounts.

“What it will mean is that millions of people have a higher balance at retirement simply because they'll be receiving their superannuation payments earlier and more frequently,” he said.

Supporters argue more frequent contributions could improve long-term balances through compounding returns, particularly for younger workers.

Koval said the reform could also help workers identify unpaid super sooner by making it easier to compare contributions arriving in their account against their payslip.

Business groups have welcomed the intent of the reform but warned the transition may create operational and cashflow challenges, particularly for small and medium-sized businesses.

Koval said while some businesses may face an adjustment period, the reform had been planned for several years and did not increase the amount employers pay , only how often payments are made.

summary.en: Canada will gain access to an Australian over-the-horizon radar system that has been in service for over 40 years.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia has struck its largest defence export deal under a $2.5 billion agreement to provide Canada with world-leading radar technology, as US allies look to broaden their security relationships.

The landmark pact was signed in Canberra on Monday by Defence Minister Richard Marles and Canada's secretary of state for defence procurement Stephen Fuhr.

"Today's agreement really is a historic moment for Australia's defence industry, but it is also a historic moment in the bilateral relationship between Australia and Canada," Marles said.

Canada will use Australia's Jindalee Operational Radar Network, known as JORN, to surveil vast swathes of the Arctic.

The over-the-horizon system has been in service for 40 years, with the system able to detect aircraft and ships up to 3,000km from the northern Australian coast.

Fuhr pointed to both nations being Commonwealth countries and Five Eyes partners, an intelligence-sharing arrangement.

"We've stood shoulder to shoulder for generations as the world adjusts to its new strategic and economic realities," he said.

"We'll continue to work with the Americans. That's not going to change, but the relationship is different.

"We have great partners in other places in the world, this being a very good example of it with this radar, and I'm sure there'll be much, much more to do."

Australia and Canada will continue working towards establishing a status of forces agreement, a legal framework which allows militaries to operate in each other's countries.

Marles said the "exquisite" radar technology would only be shared with Australia's most trusted partners.

"That said, under our government, we have looked to be more ambitious in terms of finding opportunities to engage in defence industry exports and this is something that we can do with a close friend," he said.

As Australia and Germany remain locked in talks about the potential export of the nation's Ghost Bat drone, the Canadian secretary confirmed he will also examine the locally designed aircraft.

"Collaborative combat aircraft are a thing, and it seems like Australia has got a bit of a lead there, so I'm curious to see where that's at."

Federal governments have poured more than $2.3 billion into the Ghost Bat's development since 2019, with the "loyal wingman" designed to join fighter jets in battle.

The drone is the first combat aircraft to be designed and made in Australia in 50 years.

Asked how negotiations were progressing with Germany, Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy said the government was "very confident" in the capability.

body.en:
Australia is on high alert after a second bird tested positive for a deadly strain of avian flu, raising concerns the virus may be spreading in remote locations.

A brown skua and a northern giant petrel had tested positive for the H5N1 strain of the flu after they were found in Western Australia, federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins confirmed on Monday.

There has been no evidence of mass mortalities among birds, with both animals discovered on a remote beach in Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

"We are working to determine whether or not the H5 bird flu has established in the wildlife or established in Australia, other than these two isolated birds," Ms Collins told reporters.

The poultry and agricultural sectors are free from the flu, with samples of the infected birds to be investigated over the next week.

Australians will take a long lunch this Friday to watch the Socceroos' final group-stage match as the team faces Paraguay for a spot in the knockouts.

Will Nestory Irankunda and Connor Metcalfe repeat their goalscoring success against Türkiye? Can Patrick Beach save Australia's chance at surviving the group stage?

Or will Paraguay take the lead, as midfielder Matías Galarza delivered on Saturday when his aggressive goal just 64 seconds after the starting whistle sent Türkiye packing their bags?

If the Socceroos achieve this, they'll face the runner-up in Group G — either Egypt or Iran.

If Australia loses on Friday, there's still a chance it can qualify under new rules introduced by FIFA, which will see eight teams ranked third in their group go through to the knockout stages.

In that case, the Socceroos would face the winner of either Group E, Group I, or Group K.
